output.brief: The rejects come from an interaction. Arnholt resin arrives wetter than Quillan, about 0.27–0.33% moisture against a 0.20% limit once dried. Dryer D5 is also degraded, with a dew point of about −16 to −19 instead of −40. D5 handles Quillan acceptably, at about 0.9% rejects. It cannot dry Arnholt, which gives about 10% rejects on Press 5. Arnholt on Press 7 (good dryer) runs at 0.8%. The same Arnholt lot dried in a good portable dryer gave 0.8% rejects, against 10.4% through D5. The new operators are not the cause: their reject rates match experienced operators on each resin. Second shift looks worse only because all its VX runs on Press 5. The trial missed this because it ran on Press 7 only. Don't discipline the operators, and don't drop Arnholt outright. This week: repair D5 (heater and desiccant), restore the −40 alarm limit, and keep Arnholt off D5 until it is verified. Add a feed-throat moisture check for every lot. The cause of Arnholt's higher inlet moisture (the north annex or the supplier) is unresolved, since the annex and supplier are confounded. Check that before paying for warehouse changes. Confidence is high.
